## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Primitives
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Primitive interface obligations
//  - The derived array surface
//  - The derived Integer surface
//  - The derived Number surface

library Primitives
{
    //==
    // # Primitive interface obligations
    //
    // The handful of members the `primitive` declarations in `primitives.plato` owe
    // their interface lists but that the host contract does NOT supply. Everything a
    // backend must implement natively is in `intrinsics.library.plato`; what is left
    // is derivable in Plato from those intrinsics, so it belongs here rather than
    // growing the porting checklist:
    //
    //   * the two identity conversions (`Number.ToNumber`, `Integer.ToInteger`),
    //     which exist so a body generic over `IReal` or `IWhole` can name the carrier;
    //   * `Number.Inverse` and the two `Lerp`s, one-line formulas over arithmetic
    //     the host already provides;
    //   * `Boolean.LessThanOrEquals`, read off the `Compare` intrinsic (false orders
    //     before true).
    //
    // Without these the generated members throw, so every derived body that reaches
    // them — and `IReal`/`IWhole`-generic code reaches ToNumber/ToInteger constantly —
    // throws with it.

    //==
    // # Number

    // The number itself: `IReal.ToNumber` on the carrier type is the identity.
    // It exists so a body generic over IReal can drop to a plain Number.
    ToNumber(self: Number): Number
        => self;

    // The multiplicative inverse, one over x. Division by zero yields an
    // infinity rather than signalling, as everywhere else in this vocabulary.
    Inverse(self: Number): Number
        => 1.0 / self;

    // Linear interpolation; t is unclamped, so 0 yields a, 1 yields b, and values
    // outside [0, 1] extrapolate.
    Lerp(a: Number, b: Number, t: Number): Number
        => a + (b - a) * t;

    //==
    // # Integer

    // The integer itself: `IWhole.ToInteger` on the carrier type is the identity.
    ToInteger(self: Integer): Integer
        => self;

    // Linear interpolation carried out in Number and truncated back to Integer,
    // so the result steps rather than rounding to nearest. t is unclamped.
    Lerp(a: Integer, b: Integer, t: Number): Integer
        => (a.ToNumber + (b.ToNumber - a.ToNumber) * t).ToInteger;

    //==
    // # Boolean
    //
    // And / Or / Not are the whole host contract (plato-378); everything else
    // on Boolean is a formula over them. Compare is NOT redeclared here — the
    // IOrderable generic in `core.library.plato` covers it, and
    // reading the order off Compare (as this file used to) would now recurse.

    // The truth ordering: false orders before true. a <= b holds unless a is
    // true and b is false.
    LessThanOrEquals(a: Boolean, b: Boolean): Boolean
        => !a || b;

    // Structural equality: both true, or both false.
    Equals(a: Boolean, b: Boolean): Boolean
        => (a && b) || (!a && !b);

    // Exclusive or: true when the two differ.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exclusive_or)
    ExclusiveOr(a: Boolean, b: Boolean): Boolean
        => !a.Equals(b);

    // The digest of a truth value: 1 for true, 0 for false.
    Hash(self: Boolean): Integer
        => self ? 1 : 0;

    //==
    // # The derived array surface
    //
    // Reference bodies for everything that used to be an Array / Array2D / Array3D
    // host intrinsic (plato-378). The kernel left in `intrinsics.library.plato` is
    // four functions — `Count`, `At`, `MapRange`, `Reduce` — plus `FlatMap`;
    // everything here is a reindexing of `MapRange` or a fold over `Reduce`.
    //
    // These define the SEMANTICS. A backend that has a faster native form
    // (Ara3D.Collections.Slice, std::span, a GLSL swizzle) substitutes it through
    // its override table (plato-368) rather than by re-adding an intrinsic. Without
    // that table every derived view below costs a closure per element on C#, so the
    // override table is a prerequisite for adopting this file in a hot path, not an
    // optimization on top of it.
    //
    // Bodies beside a declaration file, per LIBRARIES.md ground rule 1: the sibling
    // declarations are `primitives.plato` (Array) and
    // `primitives.types.plato` (Array2D / Array3D).

    //==
    // # Array — mapping

    // A new Array holding f applied to each element in index order.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Map_(higher-order_function))
    Map(xs: Array<$T1>, f: Function1<$T1, $T2>): Array<$T2>
        => MapRange(xs.Count, i => f(xs[i]));

    // f applied to each disjoint adjacent PAIR: elements 0-1, 2-3, and so on.
    // Trailing elements that do not fill a pair are dropped.
    MapPairs(xs: Array<$T>, f: Function2<$T, $T, $TR>): Array<$TR>
        => MapRange(xs.Count / 2, i => f(xs[i * 2], xs[i * 2 + 1]));

    // f applied to each disjoint adjacent TRIPLE. Trailing remainder dropped.
    MapTriplets(xs: Array<$T>, f: Function3<$T, $T, $T, $TR>): Array<$TR>
        => MapRange(xs.Count / 3, i => f(xs[i * 3], xs[i * 3 + 1], xs[i * 3 + 2]));

    // f applied to each disjoint adjacent QUARTET. Trailing remainder dropped.
    MapQuartets(xs: Array<$T>, f: Function4<$T, $T, $T, $T, $TR>): Array<$TR>
        => MapRange(xs.Count / 4, i => f(xs[i * 4], xs[i * 4 + 1], xs[i * 4 + 2], xs[i * 4 + 3]));

    // f applied to matching pairs from two arrays, stopping at the shorter one.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convolution_(computer_science))
    Zip(xs: Array<$T1>, ys: Array<$T2>, f: Function2<$T1, $T2, $T3>): Array<$T3>
        => MapRange(xs.Count.Lesser(ys.Count), i => f(xs[i], ys[i]));

    // f applied to matching triples from three arrays, stopping at the shortest.
    Zip(xs: Array<$T1>, ys: Array<$T2>, zs: Array<$T3>, f: Function3<$T1, $T2, $T3, $T4>): Array<$T4>
        => MapRange(xs.Count.Lesser(ys.Count).Lesser(zs.Count), i => f(xs[i], ys[i], zs[i]));

    //==
    // # Array — sub-ranges
    //
    // Every one is a MapRange whose callback shifts or scales the index.
    // Since TKT-350 (2026-10) MapRange is EAGER, so each one ALLOCATES AND FILLS
    // a new array of its window; none is a view. (Before that, "none copies" was
    // true: the array was lazy.) None validates — the preconditions are the
    // caller's, as everywhere in this vocabulary.

    // The first n elements. Precondition: 0 <= n <= Count.
    Take(xs: Array<$T>, n: Integer): Array<$T>
        => MapRange(n, i => xs[i]);

    // Every element after the first n. Precondition: 0 <= n <= Count.
    Skip(xs: Array<$T>, n: Integer): Array<$T>
        => MapRange(xs.Count - n, i => xs[i + n]);
```
